_WHAT_THIS_IS: The record of WHICH on-chain verifier the checked-in client prover blob is allowed to talk to.
packages/stark-prover/wasm/p01_stark_bg.wasm and its four inlined twins are the prover every
client actually runs. The proof wire format is agreed with the on-chain verifier and NOTHING on
the wire declares which generation produced a proof. A client that is one generation ahead of the
deployed program does not fail to build, does not fail to parse and does not fail early: it fails
at the very END of a long chunked proof upload, on chain, with FriFoldCheckFailed. That reads as an
unexplained transaction failure, which is why this file exists.
scripts/deployed-verifier-check.mjs compares the checked-in blob against this record and fails the
build when they are not compatible. It is wired into the client build and publish steps, not only CI:
MEASURED 2026-07-30, the script has seven invocations in the repo (.github/workflows/ci.yml, the
apps/web and apps/extension `build` scripts, apps/mobile `eas-build-post-install`, and the
and all seven pass `--verify-onchain --cluster devnet`. None of them runs the record-only half on its
own, and none of them sets P01_ALLOW_LOCAL_VERIFIER_GATE.
_HOW_TO_MAKE_THE_GATE_GREEN: There is exactly ONE legitimate way, and it is not an edit to this file:
1. Deploy the CURRENT programs/p01_stark_verifier to devnet.
2. Re-measure this record from the chain:
node packages/stark-prover/scripts/deployed-verifier-check.mjs --measure --cluster devnet
That prints a fresh `deployed` block read straight off the programdata account.
3. Paste the measured block in, and set deployed.accepts_client_blob_sha256 to the sha256 of the
blob you proved against that deployment.
4. Re-run the gate with the on-chain leg:
node packages/stark-prover/scripts/deployed-verifier-check.mjs --verify-onchain --cluster devnet
EDITING deployed.proof_format_generation WITHOUT REDEPLOYING IS THE FAILURE MODE THIS FILE EXISTS TO
PREVENT. It makes the offline half green and every proof still fails on chain. --verify-onchain
catches exactly that: it refetches the programdata account, recomputes deployed.elf_sha256, and
re-derives the generation from the deployed bytes.
Three fields of the `deployed` block below are therefore NOT believed, they are refetched:
elf_sha256, last_deployed_slot and proof_format_generation. Editing them does not survive the
on-chain leg. Nor can this file redirect that leg. THE CLUSTER IS THE CALLER'S, passed as
--cluster; the endpoint comes from a table in the script and the program id from Anchor.toml; and
`cluster` and `program_id` below are cross-checked against those, with either disagreeing a hard
failure. A cluster the script cannot reach is a hard failure whenever nothing else was going to fail
the run. The gate accepts --cluster devnet and --cluster mainnet-beta as LABELS; mainnet-beta then
hard-fails today for a structural reason, because Anchor.toml [programs.mainnet] carries no
p01_stark_verifier at all, so the label resolves to an endpoint but not to a program and there is
nothing to fetch (MEASURED 2026-07-31, exit 1). devnet is the only cluster this gate can currently
produce any verdict about. localnet is refused unless a human sets P01_ALLOW_LOCAL_VERIFIER_GATE=1,
and that path prints NOT A SHIPPING VERDICT, never the word PASS, and is refused anyway when CI is
set. Note what that path does NOT do: it exits 0. The banner is for a human reading the output, and
a shell chaining on `&&` sees a success. It takes both an explicit --cluster localnet and the
environment variable to reach it, and no invocation in this repo passes either (MEASURED
2026-07-31, all three variants: no variable exit 1, variable set exit 0 with LOCAL OK, variable set
under CI=true exit 1).
ONE FIELD IS BELIEVED, NOT VERIFIED: deployed.accepts_client_blob_sha256. Nothing on chain records
which client blob a deployment accepts, so no script can check it. It is a human attestation that
someone submitted a proof from that exact blob and watched it land. Setting it without having done
that is a lie this gate cannot catch. It is currently null, which is the honest value.
The other direction is constrained too, and this was MEASURED on 2026-07-30 rather than assumed.

THE CLIENT BLOB'S GENERATION IS NO LONGER READ OFF IT, IT IS MEASURED BY RUNNING IT. That changed
on 2026-07-31 and it is the reason the rest of this section reads as history.
Until then both sides were classified by scanning for panic and msg! literals that B1 introduced.
Text is editable, and it was measured editable in four consecutive rounds. The last of them:
rewriting one byte inside each of the three B1 markers in the blob — four bytes of panic text,
identical 211,370-byte length, WebAssembly.validate still true, all seven controls still present —
then `stark-wasm-twins.mjs --write` and this record pointed at the new hash, printed 'PASS - the
shipped prover matches the devnet deployment, and the chain was asked and agreed' at exit 0 while
devnet was still pre-B1 and the blob was still B1 in every way that reaches the chain.
stark-wasm-twins.mjs --check passed on the doctored set too, because the five artifacts still agreed
with each other. Adding a scan of stark/src/compact.rs, and then of the verifier crate, only raised
the price: renaming three literals in compact.rs plus ONE msg! line in verify.rs (that line carries
both literals the deployed-ELF scan uses) restored the agreement and greened the gate again, also
measured. No adversary was needed for any of it: rewording those messages during an ordinary
refactor has exactly the same effect and no warning.
What replaced it: scripts/prover-behaviour.mjs generates seven proofs with the checked-in blob, one
per shipping circuit, on seven fixed witnesses, and sha256s each. The generation is whichever column
of its fixture table all seven digests match; a mixture, or a digest in neither column, refuses to
classify and fails. B1 is length-preserving on all seven circuits — MEASURED, the B1 blob and the
bytes — so length was never going to separate them and the content digests are the discriminator.
MEASURED 2026-07-31 against the fixed gate: the identical doctored blob still emits all seven B1
digests, so it classifies b1, and the run exits 1 with 'the blob PROVES one generation and its panic
strings CLAIM another' plus the FriFoldCheckFailed interlock underneath. Renaming every literal in
the tree and in the artifact leaves the verdict where it was. It costs about 5 seconds per run.
The seven B1 digests are pinned in three files, not one: scripts/prover-behaviour.mjs,
src/wireFormat.test.ts (Pin.sha256) and programs/p01_stark_verifier/tests/b1_deep_binding.rs
(FIXTURE_C*_SHA256). The gate checks the other two at run time and refuses to classify if they no
longer carry the same digests, so moving the reference is not a one-file edit either.
What this does NOT prove: that the blob is B1 on every input. Seven witnesses is a sample. A blob
rigged to recognise those seven and replay pre-B1 proof bytes for them would read as pre-B1 — that
is a second prover or ~486 KB of canned proofs inside an artifact whose byte count is recorded here
and whose twins are hashed, not a four-byte edit, but it is not impossible.
The marker strings the gate scans for are HARDCODED in deployed-verifier-check.mjs, not read from
this file, so weakening the evidence blocks below cannot weaken the scan. They are reproduced here
for a human reader. The blob's markers are now corroboration only; the DEPLOYED side still has
nothing but them, and that asymmetry is stated in the deployed block below.
One more thing the gate did not check until then: it resolved the program id from Anchor.toml, and
no client reads Anchor.toml. Every client resolves the verifier through PROGRAM_IDS in
packages/privacy-sdk/src/constants.ts, generated from Anchor.toml by scripts/sync-program-ids.ts —
and `pnpm check-program-ids`, which would catch those drifting apart, is NOT run by
.github/workflows/ci.yml (MEASURED 2026-07-31). A second, B1 copy of the verifier deployed under a
different id, with Anchor.toml pointed at it, would have satisfied the entire on-chain leg while
every shipped client kept talking to the pre-B1 id. Both files are now read and required to agree.

DEPLOYMENTS ON DEVNET under the same upgrade authority, measured with --measure on 2026-07-31:
EXmAQqm... slot 456289287, elf 780,249 B, sha c359ab53...; DGY37k3... slot 469197514, elf
817,617 B, sha c1a26c17.... DGY37k3... is also what declare_id! in
programs/p01_stark_verifier/src/lib.rs names. Both are pre-B1, so the interlock verdict is the
same either way; the gate was still vouching for a deployment one shipped code path does not
address. Every module-level *STARK_VERIFIER* constant in the SDK is swept now and must equal
the Anchor.toml id, which is why this gate currently reports that divergence as a second
failure alongside the generation skew.
That residual is now CLOSED, and here is the whole of what closing it means. It was: renaming the
three B1 literals in stark/src/compact.rs AND the msg! line in programs/p01_stark_verifier/src/
verify.rs, with the same four bytes edited in the blob, made every source in this tree agree that it
was pre-B1 and printed the full PASS at exit 0 against the genuinely pre-B1 devnet deployment
(MEASURED 2026-07-31). The same cheat, replayed byte for byte against the fixed gate on the same
day, exits 1. Behaviour is what closed it, exactly as that finding predicted.
What is left, stated plainly rather than implied away, because a guardrail that oversells itself is
the same class of defect as the one it guards: the DEPLOYED side is still classified by scanning the
on-chain ELF for msg! literals. Nothing in a build script can run a BPF program, and submitting a
real proof to it needs funding and a ~78 KB chunked upload, so there is no behavioural classifier
available for that side. ELF_B1_MARKERS is therefore the softest thing left in this gate: pointing
those two literals at a string the pre-B1 deployment also carries would make the chain read b1.
That is bounded, not closed. KNOWN_ELF_GENERATIONS in deployed-verifier-check.mjs pins the sha256
of both live devnet deployments with the generation each was measured to be by hand (MEASURED
469197514; neither carries either B1 marker, both carry all four controls). If the chain hands back
those exact bytes it is still that deployment, so a marker scan reading one of them as b1 is two
readings of the same bytes disagreeing, and that is a hard failure. The record names the same hash,
so the contradiction is caught offline too. A pin can only ever add a failure: after a redeploy the
hash is new, nothing is pinned about it, and the scan is the only evidence again until someone
measures it and adds it.
What is left is an edit to the guardrail itself - rewording ELF_B1_MARKERS and deleting a measured
constant that names the program, the slot and the byte count it came from. That is a louder diff
than a panic-message rename buried in a refactor. It is not the same as impossible.

deployed._note: The address, slot, size and hash fields here were MEASURED off the chain on the date below and are regenerated with --measure after a deploy; do not hand-edit them. Two exceptions --measure does not produce: the `_`-prefixed blocks are prose for a human, and `accepts_client_blob_sha256` is a human attestation no script can check. `cluster` IS in the --measure output, but it is only an echo of the --cluster the caller passed; see below for why it is checked rather than obeyed.
deployed._cluster_is_checked_not_obeyed: cluster does NOT select anything. The caller passes --cluster, that label selects an RPC endpoint from the CLUSTERS table in deployed-verifier-check.mjs and a program id from Anchor.toml, and the two fields below are then checked against the caller's choice: a record that names a different cluster, or a different program id than Anchor.toml carries for it, fails the run. Two rounds of the same defect are why. First the endpoint lived here as rpc_url, and a record that names its own endpoint can name one that does not answer, which combined with an unreachable endpoint being a skip let a three-field edit pass --verify-onchain with exit code 0 and the chain never contacted. Deleting rpc_url was not enough: the LABEL was still this file's to write and localnet was one of the labels, so setting cluster to localnet, program_id to the id Anchor.toml [programs.localnet] genuinely carries, generation to b1 and accepts_client_blob_sha256 to the blob's own hash, then answering getAccountInfo on 127.0.0.1:8899 with 149 fabricated bytes, printed a full PASS at exit code 0 (MEASURED 2026-07-30), and killing the listener made the same record exit 1, so the pass came from the listener alone. The forgery was not even necessary, since a real solana-test-validator answers all of it honestly, but that variant was not run and is not claimed as measured. The gate now refuses localnet outright for any run that could be a shipping verdict.

Anchor.toml now carries DGY37k3..., because that is what declare_id! in programs/p01_stark_verifier/src/lib.rs names and an Anchor program rejects every instruction with DeclaredProgramIdMismatch at any other address — so EXmAQqm... is an address a .so built from this tree can never execute at, and a record describing it was a record about a program this source cannot become. generation_evidence.method: BEHAVIOURAL. scripts/prover-behaviour.mjs instantiates this blob under Node THROUGH THE GENERATED GLUE (initSync) and generates one proof per shipping circuit on eight fixed witnesses. The three unmasked circuits (C0, C2, C4) are judged by proof sha256; the five masked circuits (C1, C3, C5, C6, C7) draw a fresh CSPRNG mask per proof and are judged by exact proof LENGTH, pinned in src/wireFormat.test.ts. The generation is the column that ALL EIGHT rows match; a mixture, an unrecognised digest, a refusal or a wrong length is UNCLASSIFIABLE and fails the gate.
generation_evidence._previous_b1_digests: The eight rows above are the B2 column (three digests, five lengths). The B1 column this block used to carry, for whoever needs to recognise the older artifact: C0 45001 B e4aad105..., C1 65801 B 935d918c..., C2 66681 B 063d86a1..., C3 75637 B 2d97f56f..., C4 78377 B f8778367..., C5 76357 B 78afe9bb..., C6 78517 B 8e1166f5.... All seven are still pinned as the `b1` column of the fixture table in scripts/prover-behaviour.mjs, so the gate can still name a B1 blob rather than merely refusing to classify it.
generation_evidence.why_not_length: B1 changed WHAT FRI FOLDS without adding or removing a byte. MEASURED 2026-07-31 by driving both blobs: the pre-B1 blob 5fe610c9 and the B1 blob emit the SAME SEVEN LENGTHS, to the byte (45,001 / 65,801 / 66,681 / 75,637 / 78,377 / 76,357 / 78,517), and SEVEN DIFFERENT DIGESTS. Between those two generations content is the only discriminator there is. B2 is different — it widens three wire fields, so the seven lengths DID move (to the numbers above) — but that is not licence to classify on length: a blob can be given any length and only content is expensive to fake, so the verdict stays on the digest and the length stays an observation.
generation_evidence.corroboration: The three B2 digests and five masked lengths above are pinned independently in packages/stark-prover/src/wireFormat.test.ts (Pin.sha256, driving this blob) and in programs/p01_stark_verifier/tests/b1_deep_binding.rs (FIXTURE_C*_SHA256, computed from the Rust prover over the same seven witnesses). The gate reads both files and refuses to classify if either stops carrying them, so the reference cannot be moved in one file.

string_scan_kept_as_corroboration.method: byte scan of the blob for panic and assert message literals, split by ERA, controlled by domain-separation tags present in every generation. This DECIDES NOTHING. It is kept because it catches two things the digests are silent about — a string-stripped artifact, and an artifact that was not built from the source in this tree — and because a blob that proves one generation while its strings claim another is the measured four-byte edit and gets named as such.
string_scan_kept_as_corroboration._era_split_2026_08_02: The four literals used to be ONE list called BLOB_B1_MARKERS, with the scan returning 'b1' if ANY of them hit. Two of the four are [B2]-only strings, so on a correct B2 tree the scan said 'b1' while the blob proved 'b2' and the check named 'the blob PROVES one generation and its panic strings CLAIM another' fired on an honest artifact, with a remedy ('reship the blob from this tree') that could never clear it. Now BLOB_MARKERS_B1 and BLOB_MARKERS_B2 are separate and the scan is a real three-way discriminator: pre-B1 carries neither, B1 carries the first, B2 carries both.
b1_era_markers_present: DEEP denominator vanishes at LDE position
string_scan_kept_as_corroboration._deleted_marker: 'break the committed-vector/ood_quotient agreement B1 depends on' was listed here and is GONE from the source and therefore from the blob. It was the message on the `q_poly.len() <= lde_size` assert in the six quotient builders; B2 replaced that guarantee with the two segment_quotient_poly asserts above, which are the strings that now carry the same job.
string_scan_kept_as_corroboration._merged_2026_08_03: Two lots split this list independently on 2026-08-02 and the merge kept ONE of them, not a blend: BLOB_MARKERS_B1 / BLOB_MARKERS_B2 in deployed-verifier-check.mjs, with classifyBlob requiring the WHOLE B2 era before it says b2. The other lot's classifyBlobStrings said b2 on any single B2 marker and is deleted; the difference is recorded on BLOB_MARKERS_B2. The deployed-ELF side is NOT two-valued as that lot's note said: classifyElf answers 'b1+' when it can only see 'B1 or newer', and generationsAreCompatible is what compares it. See deployed.generation_evidence.this_scan_cannot_say_b2.

string_scan_kept_as_corroboration._controls_shrunk_2026_08_03: bnd-c5 and bnd-c6 were in the list above and were REMOVED, because a CORRECT build of this tree no longer emits them and the remedy the gate printed ('reship the blob') could never have cleared it. That is the second time a byte scan here fired on an honest artifact -- see _era_split_2026_08_02 for the first. MEASURED over both blobs, raw byte occurrences of all six boundary tags: old (2a962ca9) had bnd-c1 1, bnd-c3 1, bnd-c5 1, bnd-c6 1 and bnd-c2 0, bnd-c4 0 -- exactly the four circuits that HAD a boundary fold; new (2613ffed) has all six at 0, while rlc-c1/c2/c3/c5 and proof_hex are untouched, so nothing was stripped. CAUSE: commit 109a4aa6, the C2/C4 binding fix, routed all six tags through one match returning *b"bnd-cN\0\0" BY VALUE as [u8;8]; a value needs no address, so LLVM emits immediates instead of a data-segment constant, and the only surviving by-reference use is inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests, which no wasm-pack build sees. PROOF THE BEHAVIOUR DID NOT MOVE WITH THE STRINGS: C5 and C6 emit proofs byte-identical to the pre-fold blob (28ef7176, b8dc81e0), impossible if their tag had stopped being absorbed, and C2/C4 match the digests the Rust prover pins independently. The presence of a tag STRING is a codegen artifact, not a semantic invariant; what remains in the list is a stripped-artifact canary and nothing more.
